result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.add_star_graph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Add a star graph (hub-and-spoke) to the current graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L3248-L3317){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.add_star_graph( n, type=None, label=True, rel=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Star graph](/assets/graphs/add-star-graph.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Three star graphs side by side: a hub with three spokes for n=4, four spokes for n=5, and six spokes for n=7. The hub is joined to every other node and the spokes are not joined to each other, so n nodes give n - 1 edges." width="100%"} Creates a central hub node connected to `n - 1` peripheral nodes. All edges connect the hub to spokes; no edges between spokes. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [n]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Total number of nodes (minimum `2`). [type]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional node type/category for all nodes. [label]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, label nodes with their IDs. [rel]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional relationship label for all edges. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} A star graph has one hub connected to every other node, with no edges between the spokes themselves -- so `n` nodes always produce exactly `n - 1` edges: ::: {#83d0d344 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph().add_star_graph(n=5) # 1 hub + 4 spokes graph.count_nodes(), graph.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (5, 4) ``` ::: :::
